references.text: Abimelech, Gideon's son, attempts to establish the kingdom that Gideon rejected, illustrating the consequences of the people's desire for a ruler.
Israel asks Samuel for a king, reflecting the same desire for human rule that the Israelites expressed to Gideon.
Samuel reminds the people that the Lord is their king, just as Gideon also pointed out in his response to them.
Gideon's response to the people's request, where he refuses to rule and declares that the Lord shall rule over them.
David wishes to build a temple for the Lord after God has given him victory over his enemies, paralleling Gideon's victory over the Midianites.
The description of the victory over the Midianites that led to the people's desire for Gideon to rule over them.
